clue.text: Healing influence spoken of in castle

parts.note: balm is a soothing ointment, anything with a healing influence
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A soothing, restorative presence is talked about inside some castle.
explanation.walkthrough: BALMORAL is the British royal family's castle in Scotland; 'of' and 'in' are only joining words here.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral is a royal residence in Aberdeenshire, a castle by name.

parts.note: disarming normally means charming, but read literally it is removing someone's arm, which a surgeon does in an operation

explanation.definitionFit: To cut off a limb surgically is literally to dis-arm a patient, the operation being the performance.

clue.text: But an MP of the centre may hold it

definitions.text: But an MP of the centre may hold it

parts.words: But an MP of the centre may hold it
parts.note: the clue reads as a political middle-ground figure, but it describes a constituency won by a narrow margin, which any MP may hold only just

explanation.walkthrough: The 'centre' suggests middle-of-the-road politics; the joke is that a seat on the margin is the opposite of central, yet a centrist MP may still hold one.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituency held by a slim majority, so on the edge of changing hands, is described by this political term.

clue.text: Back later, about one, for sale

indicators.note: about places the following item inside, surrounded by the turned word
back tells us to read the word later from end to start

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Come back later, at around one o'clock, if you want to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns LATER into RETAL, and 'about' puts I (one) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail describes goods sold to the public, the trade of offering things for sale.

indicators.note: receives means the boy takes in the note, enclosing it

parts.note: lad is an informal word for a boy

explanation.surface: A rural lad gets a letter in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Land can mean a nation or realm, as in a foreign land.

parts.note: Oz suggests Australia, but the land of Oz is home to a famous conjuror whose craft is a tricky performance

explanation.walkthrough: Oz looks like slang for Australia; it is the land of Oz, where the title character of The Wizard of Oz performs his tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic or conjuring, a display of tricks, is the art of a sorcerer such as the one in Oz.

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Fasten a rope firmly to a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash something is to bind it fast with rope or cord.

parts.note: snaps are thin crisp biscuits, as in ginger snaps
food just out of the oven is hot

explanation.surface: An image of biscuits just baked.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph, a quick picture.

parts.note: acid can mean sharp or sour in taste
rain is a fall of water from the sky

explanation.surface: A steep drop in pollution levels.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain made acidic by industrial emissions is a familiar form of environmental pollution.

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for hits from end to start

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks or hits

explanation.surface: A boxer strikes back in a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or fight, especially in practice.

clue.text: Daily's joint role as substitute parent

parts.note: the Guardian is a British daily newspaper, here with its possessive
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A newspaper's shared position on fostering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' is a crossword favourite for a newspaper; here THE GUARDIAN, a London daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Guardianship is the legal care of a child by someone acting in place of a parent.

parts.note: a confidence is a secret told quietly, but in a theatre this whispered aside is meant to be heard by the entire audience

explanation.walkthrough: 'House' looks domestic; in theatre it means the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's loud aside, supposedly private, is heard by every seat in the auditorium.

clue.text: Relative with pound goes in to get glove

indicators.note: goes in to means the relative and the pound are put inside the next word

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A relative brings money in order to buy a glove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes in to' puts AUNT and L inside GET, which the clue gives as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauntlet is a stout glove, often with a long cuff, as worn by knights.

clue.text: Be behind, right in the back

indicators.note: in places the letter for right inside the word for the back

parts.note: the tail is the back or rear end of something

explanation.surface: Lagging behind, with the right side at the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail is to lag or follow some way after others.

indicators.note: broke out suggests the letters of hatred burst apart and re-form

explanation.surface: During a famine, enmity erupted.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity, and famine is an extreme scarcity of food.

clue.text: Beautiful girl, say, that's likely to get a ring

definitions.text: that's likely to get a ring

indicators.note: say signals that the word for a beautiful girl is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful girl or woman

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman is likely to receive an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring looks like an engagement ring; a bell is rung.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell gets rung, so it is the thing to get a ring.

clue.text: Primate born in cove under shrub

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, puts the cove piece below the shrub

parts.note: a bush is a shrub

indicators.note: in places the letter for born inside the word for cove

parts.note: a bay is a cove or inlet of the sea

explanation.surface: A monkey born in a sheltered inlet beneath a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushbaby, or galago, is a small nocturnal African primate.

definitions.meaning: ... about something means enthusiastic about it
... paving is made of irregular broken slabs fitted together

explanation.walkthrough: Crazy paving is a garden path or patio of irregular, broken flagstones, a common British garden feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy means wildly enthusiastic, and crazy paving is the irregular patio style.

parts.note: a con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
to tempt someone is to entice or provoke them

explanation.surface: A convict goads others into scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt is scorn, the feeling behind derision.

clue.text: Eleven seized by extraterrestrial? Way out!

indicators.note: seized by means the number is held inside the alien

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Eleven people abducted by an alien: how bizarre!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way out!' reads as slang for weird, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a way out of a building or space.

definitions.note: Saint's is read as Saint is, the 's a joining word

indicators.note: being tailored suggests the letters are cut and remade into a new form

explanation.surface: A holy man is against having his suit altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agin' is dialect for against; here it is just letters, mixed with SUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: St Ignatius of Loyola, founder of the Jesuits, is one of several saints of this name.

definitions.meaning: to cover is to shield or conceal
films are projected on the large white surface at the front

explanation.definitionFit: A screen hides or shelters something, and is also the surface on which films are shown.

clue.text: Parted with worker that's literally sinister

parts.note: if you parted with somewhere, you left it
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Separated from an employee who is quite evil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' means evil, but its Latin root means on the left side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister comes from the Latin word for the side opposite the right, so it literally means that side.

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a clothes horse is a frame for drying laundry, also called an airer

explanation.surface: A good horse with a paler coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' looks like an animal; it is a clothes horse, a frame for drying washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairer means paler, of a lighter skin or hair colour.

clue.text: A swift bottle drunk, then keen debate

indicators.note: drunk suggests the words are in a muddled state and reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone downs a bottle fast, then argues hotly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges the letters of A SWIFT BOTTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest of wit, a sharp exchange of clever arguments, is a lively debate.

clue.text: African country also has good interior

indicators.note: has means the word for also holds the next letter
interior means the letter for good sits within the word for also

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: An African state also has a good interior.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a small West African nation on the Gulf of Guinea.

indicators.note: we hear signals the word for illness is heard and spelt differently

parts.note: flu is a common illness

explanation.surface: Someone fled from a sickness, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Flew is the past of fly, meaning rushed or hurried away.

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Correct parking, right by the kerb.
explanation.definitionFit: Prim means stiffly correct and formal in manner.

clue.text: Great-Granny Smith found in New York

parts.note: big means great
a Granny Smith is a variety of apple

explanation.surface: Grandma's mother Smith turns up in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great-Granny' reads as a great-grandmother; split it into Great and Granny Smith, the green apple.
explanation.definitionFit: New York City has long been nicknamed after a large fruit.

definitions.note: Jailer's is read as Jailer is, the 's a joining word

parts.note: war is battle or armed conflict
dress means uniform, as in military dress

explanation.surface: A prison officer's combat kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardress was a female prison officer, a jailer.
